title: Erdős–Hajnal Independence Number Problem
statement_text: Determine the minimum independence number of a 3-uniform hypergraph on $N$ vertices in which there are at most two edges among any four vertices; equivalently, determine $r(K_4^{(3)}\setminus e,\, K_n^{(3)})$.
context_text: In 1972, Erdős and Hajnal posed this problem and showed the answer lies between $\Omega(\log N/\log\log N)$ and $O(\log N)$, i.e., in the Ramsey-number language $2^{\Omega(n)} \le r(K_4^{(3)}\setminus e, K_n^{(3)}) \le n^{O(n)}$. The problem received considerable attention over the subsequent half-century; Mubayi and Suk described it as 'a very interesting open problem, as $K_4^{(3)}\setminus e$ is, in some sense, the smallest 3-uniform hypergraph whose Ramsey number with a clique is at least exponential.'
paper_contribution: Proves $r(K_4^{(3)}\setminus e, K_n^{(3)}) = n^{\Theta(n)}$ (Theorem 1.1), establishing that the minimum independence number is $\Theta(\log N / \log\log N)$ and completely solving the longstanding open problem.

title: Exact Ramsey growth rate dependence on G for link hypergraphs
statement_text: It would be interesting to determine the exact dependence on $G$ in the bounds $\Omega(1/g) \le \frac{\log r(L_G,\, K_n^{(3)})}{n \log n} \le O(s)$, where $G$ is a non-bipartite graph on $s$ vertices with odd girth $g \ge 3$.
context_text: A $k$-graph is a $k$-uniform hypergraph and $K_n^{(3)}$ the complete 3-graph on $n$ vertices; the Ramsey number $r(H,K_n^{(3)})$ is the least $N$ such that every 3-graph on $N$ vertices contains a copy of $H$ or an independent set of size $n$ (no edge inside). For a graph $G$, the link hypergraph $L_G$ is the 3-graph on $V(G)\cup\{u\}$ whose edges are the triples $\{u,v,w\}$ with $vw\in E(G)$ (so $L_{K_3}=K_4^{(3)}\setminus e$); a 3-graph is $L_G$-free iff the link of each vertex (the graph of pairs forming an edge with it) is $G$-free. The odd girth of a non-bipartite graph is the length of its shortest odd cycle. Logarithms are base 2 unless noted. Conlon, Fox and Sudakov showed $r(L_G,K_n^{(3)})=n^{\Theta(1)}$ if $G$ is bipartite and $r(L_G,K_n^{(3)})\ge2^{\Omega(n)}$ otherwise. The authors prove $r(L_G,K_n^{(3)})=n^{\Theta(n)}$ for every fixed non-bipartite $G$, solving in particular the Erdős–Hajnal problem for $K_4^{(3)}\setminus e$. The lower bound comes from a random 3-graph on $n^{\Omega(n/g)}$ vertices in which every link has odd girth greater than $g$ and the complement contains no $K^{(3)}_{n,n,n}$. The upper bound is $r(L_{K_s},K_n^{(3)})<(2n)^{sn}$. Together they give the stated bounds $n^{\Omega(n/g)}\le r(L_G,K_n^{(3)})\le n^{O(sn)}$ for $G$ on $s$ vertices with odd girth $g$. The authors further conjecture that for every non-bipartite $G$ there is a constant $c_G$ with $r(L_G,K_n^{(3)})=n^{(1+o(1))c_G n}$. They note that such constants, if they exist for odd cycles $C_g$, are bounded by an absolute constant, but it is unknown whether they tend to zero. This is hypergraph Ramsey theory.

title: Determine the order of f_k(N; s, t) in general
statement_text: Determine the order of $f_k(N; s, t)$ for all valid parameters $k \ge 3$, $s \ge k+1$, and $1 \le t \le \binom{s}{k}$.
context_text: A $k$-graph is a $k$-uniform hypergraph and $K_n^{(3)}$ the complete 3-graph on $n$ vertices; the Ramsey number $r(H,K_n^{(3)})$ is the least $N$ such that every 3-graph on $N$ vertices contains a copy of $H$ or an independent set of size $n$ (no edge inside). Erdős and Hajnal defined $f_k(N;s,t)$ as the minimum possible independence number of a $k$-graph on $N$ vertices in which any $s$ vertices span fewer than $t$ edges (for example $f_3(N;4,3)$ is essentially the inverse of $r(K_4^{(3)}\setminus e,K_n^{(3)})$). For fixed $k\ge3$ and $s\ge k+1$, they conjectured that as $t$ increases from $1$ to $\binom{s}{k}$, $f_k(N;s,t)$ grows first like a power of $N$, then beyond thresholds $h_1^{(k)}(s)<h_2^{(k)}(s)<\dots$ like a power of $\log N$, of $\log\log N$, and so on, up to the $(k-2)$-fold iterated logarithm; they also conjectured the value of the first threshold. That conjecture was solved for $k=3$ and infinitely many $s$ by Conlon–Fox–Sudakov, for $k\ge4$ by Mubayi–Razborov, and for $s=k+1$ by Mubayi–Suk. Despite this, the order of $f_k(N;s,t)$ has remained wide open. The authors prove that for every fixed $s\ge4$ and $t\in(e(s),E(s)]$, $f_3(N;s,t)=\Theta(\log N/\log\log N)$. Here $e(s)\le(0.266+o(1))\binom s3$ is the maximum number of edges of a 3-graph on $s$ vertices all of whose vertex links are bipartite, and $E(s)\ge(0.464-o(1))\binom s3$ is the maximum number of edges of a 3-graph $H$ on $s$ vertices with $r(H,K_n^{(3)})=n^{O(n)}$. This is hypergraph Ramsey theory.
